**Home stadiums of the national teams that have won the last 10 UEFA European Championships (EURO)**  

| Euro (Year) | Champion | Current “home” stadium (most-used for national‑team fixtures) | City | Approx. capacity* |
|-------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|------|-------------------|
| 2024 | **Germany** | Allianz Arena | Munich | 75 000 |

| 2016 | **Portugal** | Estádio da Luz | Lisbon | 50 095 |

| 2000 | **France** | Stade de France | Saint‑Denis (Paris) | 80 697 |
| 1996 | **Germany** | Allianz Arena | Munich | 75 000 |
| 1992 | **Denmark** | Parken Stadium | Copenhagen | 38 000 |
| 1988 | **Netherlands** | De Kuip (Feijenoord Stadion) | Rotterdam | 47 235 |

\*Capacities are the current official figures (as of 2024) and reflect the maximum number of spectators the stadium can accommodate for football matches.

---

### Quick notes

- **Germany** – The Allianz Arena in Munich has been the main venue for the German national team since its opening in 2005, replacing the Olympiastadion.
- **Italy** – The historic Stadio Olimpico in Rome serves as the primary home ground for the Azzurri.
- **Portugal** – Estádio da Luz in Lisbon is the flagship stadium for the Portuguese side, having hosted several major internationals.
- **Spain** – The Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid is the traditional home of the Spanish national team and hosts most of its home fixtures.
- **Greece** – The Athens Olympic Stadium, built for the 2004 Olympics, remains Greece’s main national‑team venue.
- **France** – Stade de France in Saint‑Denis is the national stadium used for nearly all French home internationals.
- **Denmark** – Parken Stadium in Copenhagen is the modern home of the Danes.
- **Netherlands** – De Kuip (Feijenoord Stadion) in Rotterdam is the Netherlands’ main training and match venue, although matches are also played at other Dutch stadiums such as De Kuip, De Kuip, etc.  

These stadiums are the ones currently listed as the “home” or flagship venues for the respective national teams as of 2025.
